title: docs: explain UTC storage vs local report dates
body:
### Summary
Adds a "Dates and time zones" section to README.md with a fictional UTC+02:00 worked example near midnight, the half-open local-day interval, boundary clipping, and the effect of changing the machine timezone. Documentation-only: no Python changes. DST (#141) and generator options (#184) are untouched.

Closes #322

### Validation Evidence

| Environment (OS / Python) | Command or Manual Step Run | Actual Result | Reason if Skipped |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Linux 6.18.44 x86_64 / Python 3.12.3 | `python3 /tmp/check_utc_example.py` (stdlib `datetime`, `timezone(timedelta(hours=2))`; machine timezone not changed; script and full output below) | Both conversions and both day boundaries match the README; the crossing period splits 1800 s / 1800 s | |
| Linux 6.18.44 x86_64 / Python 3.12.3 | `python3 -m unittest discover -v` (system Python, no `.venv`) | Ran 96 tests, OK | |
| Linux / Python 3.12.3 | `git diff --check`; script check that `#reports-and-data`, `#command-line-tools` and `#dates-and-time-zones` match README headings; `markdown` library render of the new section | Clean; all three anchors found; table renders with 3 rows | |
| GitHub rendered preview (browser) | Opened the branch README at `#dates-and-time-zones`; followed both new links | Table and code spans render; links land on `#reports-and-data` and `#command-line-tools` | |
| Windows | `windows_desktop_smoke.py`, native walkthrough, live tracker | Not run | Documentation-only change; no interface or installer change |

Behavior references read before writing: `to_storage` and `to_utc` (timetracker/database.py), `local_midnight` and `collect_periods` (timetracker/reporting.py), `period_row` and `export_activity` (timetracker/exporting.py), and the `local_midnight` calls in windows_app.py.

Actual output of the conversion check:

```text
A: 2026-10-06T21:30:00+00:00 -> 2026-10-06T23:30:00+02:00  (local date 2026-10-06)
B: 2026-10-06T22:30:00+00:00 -> 2026-10-07T00:30:00+02:00  (local date 2026-10-07)
Oct 7 local day start in UTC: 2026-10-06T22:00:00+00:00
Oct 7 local day end   in UTC: 2026-10-07T22:00:00+00:00
A in Oct 7 interval: False
B in Oct 7 interval: True
22:00:00Z in interval (inclusive start): True
2026-10-07T22:00:00Z in interval (exclusive end): False
crossing period total: 3600.0 s; clipped into Oct 7: 1800.0 s; remaining in Oct 6: 1800.0 s
```

<details>
<summary>Script used (fictional values, fixed offset)</summary>

```python
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

local = timezone(timedelta(hours=2))  # illustrative fixed UTC+02:00

def show(label, iso):
    utc = datetime.fromisoformat(iso)
    loc = utc.astimezone(local)
    print(f"{label}: {utc.isoformat()} -> {loc.isoformat()}  (local date {loc.date()})")

show("A", "2026-10-06T21:30:00+00:00")
show("B", "2026-10-06T22:30:00+00:00")

day_start = datetime(2026, 10, 7, 0, 0, tzinfo=local)
day_end = datetime(2026, 10, 8, 0, 0, tzinfo=local)
print("Oct 7 local day start in UTC:", day_start.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat())
print("Oct 7 local day end   in UTC:", day_end.astimezone(timezone.utc).isoformat())

a = datetime.fromisoformat("2026-10-06T21:30:00+00:00")
b = datetime.fromisoformat("2026-10-06T22:30:00+00:00")
lo, hi = day_start.astimezone(timezone.utc), day_end.astimezone(timezone.utc)
print("A in Oct 7 interval:", lo <= a < hi)
print("B in Oct 7 interval:", lo <= b < hi)
print("22:00:00Z in interval (inclusive start):", lo <= datetime(2026,10,6,22,0,tzinfo=timezone.utc) < hi)
print("2026-10-07T22:00:00Z in interval (exclusive end):", lo <= datetime(2026,10,7,22,0,tzinfo=timezone.utc) < hi)

p_start = datetime.fromisoformat("2026-10-06T21:30:00+00:00")
p_end = datetime.fromisoformat("2026-10-06T22:30:00+00:00")
clip_start, clip_end = max(p_start, lo), min(p_end, hi)
print("crossing period total:", (p_end - p_start).total_seconds(), "s;",
      "clipped into Oct 7:", (clip_end - clip_start).total_seconds(), "s;",
      "remaining in Oct 6:", (min(p_end, lo) - p_start).total_seconds(), "s")
```

</details>
